correctness.rationale: The nonnegative symmetric kernel is normalized in each variable. On either side of a unit jump its error has a definite sign, so integration gives twice the cross-cut mass. Integration of the Bernstein basis gives binomial tails with m=n+1, and the tail-sum formula for two independent Bin(m,s) variables yields E_n(s)=E|X-Y|/m. Each of the m Bernoulli differences is symmetric on ±1 with probability u=s(1-s) each and is otherwise zero. Differentiating the product law leaves m times the expected integer second difference of |.|, giving 2m Pr(S_(m-1)=0)>0 for the unnormalized expectation. This includes m=1, and the strictly largest response is at s=1/2. There X-Y has law Bin(2m,1/2)-m; summing positive deviations with (j-m)binom(2m,j)=m[binom(2m-1,j-1)-binom(2m-1,j)] telescopes to m binom(2m,m)/4^m. The signed derivative representation and Fubini bound the error by the integral of jump responses against |Df|. Equality forces |Df| to be supported exclusively at the midpoint, hence exactly the stated nonzero centered jumps plus constants modulo null sets. Stirling gives the stated correction and n=0 gives 1/2. An independently written standard-library calculation (`/workspace/reproductions/bernstein.py`) checked 375 degree/location pairs through n=24, comparing Bernstein antiderivatives with the random walk conditional on its number of nonzero moves and checking the strict midpoint maximum on the test mesh. The universal assertions are analytic, not an inference from that mesh.

value.rationale: The exact coefficient calibrates the intrinsic integrated smoothing error of a canonical positive Markov kernel for every degree, not just the leading rate. The norm is actually attained, and rigidity says that only a centered discontinuity can realize it at any finite degree. Those two finite assertions furnish information that a rate or convergence of maximizing locations cannot supply.
